title: Gideon and the Ember
premise: Orsen Dunmore has spent thirty years as warden of the Hollow Gate, the last sealed door of Vessany, a kingdom erased from every map and memory except his. When a child named Ember arrives speaking Old Vessani, the gate begins to open, and Orsen learns he was never its keeper but its prisoner — bound by a bargain his father made to hide the kingdom's surviving people from a purge. Pursued by the Chancery's inquisitors who want the gate destroyed and its refugees forgotten, Orsen and Ember must cross a country that exists only in songs to reach the true door out. In the end, Orsen chooses to break his oath of silence: he testifies to what was done, trading his own belonging in the valley for the survival of everyone behind the gate.
about_author: Rafael Nakamura is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town records before turning to fiction full-time. He writes from a farmhouse in the northern hills, where he claims the fog does most of the drafting.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Routine
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. We meet his rigid, lonely life tending the Hollow Gate in a valley where magic cannot follow. He inspects seals, recites the litany, avoids the village that half-fears him. Emotional beat: contentment built on denial, cracked by a dream of a door opening.

chapters.title: A Knock in Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A mud-streaked child arrives at night, speaking a language Orsen recognizes from his father's forbidden prayer book. The gate hums for the first time in decades. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant wonder as duty collides with curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgets
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. The child reveals she walked out of the gate's far side, from a country called Vessany that Orsen was told is empty. She calls him 'the last Dunmore' with accusation in her voice. Emotional beat: Orsen's identity begins to unravel; Ember is angry, frightened, and fiercely alive.

chapters.title: The Litany of Ash
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He opens his father's hidden papers and learns the truth: Vessany wasn't destroyed, it was hidden, and the Dunmores were paid in silence. The first Chancery rider appears on the valley road. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Riders in Grey
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Inquisitor Serah Vole arrives asking polite questions about 'anomalous children.' Orsen lies badly; Ember hides in the cellar where magic cannot find her. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread, first direct threat.

chapters.title: Through the Cracked Seal
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Ember convinces Orsen to open the gate a hand's width. On the other side: a living valley, lantern-lit terraces, hundreds of hidden Vessani — and their council, who want the child returned and the stranger gone. Emotional beat: awe undercut by rejection; Orsen doesn't belong anywhere.

chapters.title: The Council of the Hidden
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Vessani elders reveal the bargain: the purge ended long ago, but the Chancery still hunts survivors to erase the crime. They refuse to leave; they demand Orsen reseal the gate forever, with Ember inside. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — safety purchased with a child's freedom.

chapters.title: Ember's Choice
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Ember refuses to be locked away again; she was sent out deliberately, carrying a key-song only she can sing. She runs back through the gate toward Orsen just as Vole's riders breach the valley. Emotional beat: defiant hope, first open violence.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Chancery burns the keeper's house and the litany records. Orsen flees with Ember into the hills, officially an outlaw now. Emotional beat: grief for the only home he knew, strangely lightened by its loss.

chapters.title: Songs of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Traveling through land that maps call wilderness but ballads call Vessany, Ember teaches Orsen the old tongue. Each place-name sung makes the landscape briefly remember itself — roads appear, ruins stand whole. Emotional beat: wonder; the past as a usable country.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge at Merrowfen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A smuggler bridge demands payment in truths. Orsen confesses his father's bargain aloud for the first time; the toll-keeper, a hidden Vessani himself, lets them pass and warns them Vole has hired a truth-reader. Emotional beat: shame shared becomes strength.

chapters.title: The Truth-Reader
chapters.summary: Vole's POV (first antagonist chapter). We see Vole's conviction: erasure is mercy, and unfinished kingdoms breed wars. She interrogates the toll-keeper and learns the fugitives' route. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy — the villain believes she is kind.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Singing Stones
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Chancery soldiers trap them among standing stones that echo the old tongue. Ember sings and the stones answer, burying the ambush in a landslide of remembered rock. But she loses her voice doing it. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Silent Road
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Ember can no longer speak the key-song. Orsen, who spent a lifetime memorizing without understanding, realizes he knows the litany well enough to carry it — if he can trust what it means. Emotional beat: quiet determination; the student becomes the vessel.

chapters.title: The City That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They reach Corvane-in-exile, the capital that persists only between dusk and dawn, populated by ghosts of the purge who mistake Orsen for his father. Emotional beat: confrontation with inherited guilt; the dead ask him why he stayed away.

chapters.title: What His Father Knew
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Among the ghost-archives Orsen finds his father's final letter: the elder Dunmore hid the gate not to protect Vessany, but because he was paid to ensure no survivor could ever testify. Emotional beat: rage and heartbreak; the oath was always a muzzle.

chapters.title: Vole Closes In
chapters.summary: Vole's POV. Vole reaches the ghost-city at dawn as it dissolves, capturing Ember when the girl lingers to free a trapped spirit. Orsen escapes alone with the key-song and no one to sing it. Emotional beat: despair, lowest point.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Ashes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen trades himself to Vole: his testimony about the purge, sworn before the Chancery tribunal, in exchange for Ember's release and safe passage for the Vessani. Vole accepts, certain a broken man will lie. Emotional beat: cold clarity; justice chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Tribunal at Greywater
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Before the tribunal, Orsen speaks the entire litany aloud — names, dates, crimes — and each true word makes the room remember: maps redraw themselves, clerks weep in a language they never learned. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth as unstoppable force.

chapters.title: The Door Out
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Freed amid the chaos, Ember finds her voice returning as the country remembers itself. She sings the key-song at the Hollow Gate while Orsen holds the Chancery off. The gate opens fully — not an escape hatch, but a doorway home. Emotional beat: exultant climax.

chapters.title: Kingdoms Remembered
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Vessani pour out into a world that now recalls them; Vole, confronted by her own tribunal's restored memory, stands down rather than deny what she witnessed. Orsen, having testified against his own blood, belongs nowhere — and is welcomed everywhere. Emotional beat: bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: The New Keeper
chapters.summary: Ember's POV, coda. Years later, Ember keeps the Hollow Gate — now a bridge, not a prison — and teaches the old tongue to travelers. Orsen lives in the valley at last, no longer warden but neighbor. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted; the door stays open.
